  "text": "The woman at the repair counter tipped the contents of the envelope onto a cloth.

“Both hands are here,” she said. “That helps.”

Martin stood his umbrella against the counter. It slid sideways, and he caught it before it fell.

“It belonged to my wife.”

The woman bent over the watch. Under her lamp, the loose hands looked like two black eyelashes.

“Water damage?”

“Washing machine.”

She glanced up.

“I forgot to check her cardigan.”

She moved the pieces apart with tweezers.

“We can replace the movement. The face has stained, though. I’d leave that alone.”

“How much?”

She wrote a figure on a pad and turned it towards him.

Martin read it twice.

“You could get a good new one for less,” she said.

“She had a good one. This was for the garden.”

There was soil caught in the buckle. He had cleaned the strap with a toothbrush but missed that bit.

“Does it need to keep time?” the woman asked.

He looked at the clocks behind her. None of them agreed.

“I suppose that’s what I came in for.”

“People sometimes only want the hands put back.”

Outside, someone knocked rain from an awning with a broom. Water splashed across the pavement.

“Fix it, please.”

She pulled a ticket from a book.

“Name?”

He gave hers, then corrected himself.

The woman crossed nothing out. She turned the ticket over and began again.

“Two weeks,” she said.

Martin tucked the receipt into his wallet. At the door, he remembered the umbrella.

When he came back, she had already set it upright beside the counter."
